input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds only Customer with a 24-month no-hire covering every Vendor employee and expressly reaching applicants "regardless of how the employee applies", i.e. no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. That is a no-hire at the outer duration limit and unlimited in scope, breaching our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer) and touching the walk-away line. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire any person responding to general recruitment. Preferred redline is deletion; fallback (offered in the comment) is a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services with advertising/unsolicited carve-outs and no no-hire.

proposal.summary: Delete the one-sided 24-month no-hire binding Customer (§ 12.4)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 12.4: our position is that Customer accepts no non-solicit or no-hire restriction, and this clause also contradicts § 12.3, which confirms Customer has made no no-hire commitment and remains free to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. If Vendor needs protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, running 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no no-hire element.
